units: Kel. XVII, 14 כְּנַף העוז things made of feathers of the sea-eagle; a. e.—Du. כְּנָפַיִם, pl. כְּנָפִים, כַּנְפוֹת.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 17:14">Ib.</cite>
<cite ref="Mishnah Tahorot 1:2">Toh. I, 2</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 3:4">Ḥull. III, 4</cite> <he>נמרטו כנָפֶיהָ</he> if the wing-feathers are plucked out, v. <cite ref="N00399"><he>נוֹצָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 3:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>כל שיש לו ארבע כ׳ … וכְנָפָיו וכ׳ …</he> that (locust) which has four feet and four wings …, and whose wings cover the larger portion of its body (is clean); a. fr.
<cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 115:2">Sifré Num. 115</cite> <he>מן הכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="C00208"><he>גְּדִילָה</he> II</cite>.
<cite ref="Sifrei Bamidbar 115:2">Ib.</cite> <he>מצות כ׳</he> the law concerning the borders of garments (<cite ref="Numbers 15:38">Num. XV, 38</cite>).—Pl. as ab.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 18:5">Lev. R. s. 18</cite>; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 12:3:1">Koh. R. to XII, 3</cite> (ref. to <he>הראות</he> <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 12:3:1">ib.</cite>) <he>אלו כַּנְפֵי הריאה</he> those are the laps (extreme ends) of the lungs.
Ḥull. 45ᵃ עד כנפי ריאה התחתונה to the borders of the lowest lung (of the animal suspended by its feet).—Euphem. for a woman’s lap (pudenda).
<cite ref="Yevamot 4a:11">Yeb. 4ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yevamot 49a:10">49ᵃ</cite> (expl.
<cite ref="Deuteronomy 23:1">Deut. XXIII, 1</cite>) <he>כ׳ שראה אביו</he> the lap which his father has seen, i.e. any woman with whom his father has had sexual connection.

senses.gloss: cover. Pesik. Zakh., p. 29ᵃ; Pesik. R. s. 12; Tanḥ. Ki Thetsé 11 (ref. to יִכָּנֵף, Is. XXX, 20) … כל זמן כ׳ מכסה וכ׳ as long as the seed of Amalek survives, it is as if a cover hid the face (of Divinity) &c.

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 7:11">Pes. VII, 11</cite> (<cite ref="Pesachim 84a:13">84ᵃ</cite>) <he>ראשי כ׳</he> the cartilaginous tops of the fore-legs.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 6:9:9">Y. Naz. VI, 55ᶜ</cite> bot. (ref. to <cite ref="Numbers 6:19">Num. VI, 19</cite>) <he>בין שיש לו כ׳ וכ׳</he> whether or not he has hands (to receive the offerings; Bab.
<cite ref="Nazir 46b:1">Naz. 46ᵇ</cite> <he>כַּפַּיִם</he>).
Tosef. Dem. II, 11 מקבלין לכ׳ we accept a ḥaber (v. חָבֵר), if he promises to observe levitical cleanness of hands; Bekh. 30ᵇ.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 2:3:6">Y. Dem. II, 23ᵃ</cite> top <he>מקריבין לכ׳</he>.
Ib. כ׳ מדפות וכ׳ the laws concerning hands, &c., v. מִדָּף.—אלישע בעל כ׳ one Elisha, a ḥaber observing cleanness of hands. Y. Ber. I, 4ᶜ bot.; Sabb. 49ᵃ; 130ᵃ (legendary origin of the surname).—
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 32:8">Lev. R. s. 32</cite> <he>בעל כ׳</he> the winged angel.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 11:6">Kel. XI, 6</cite>; Tosef.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 11:6">ib.</cite>
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 1:7">B. Mets. I, 7</cite>, v. <cite ref="O00720"><he>סִימְפּוֹנְיָא</he></cite>.

Kel. XIV, 4 הכ׳ המקבלות וכ׳ the curves on the harness for holding the reins; ib. 5 כ׳ העשוים לנוי for ornament.—Trnsf. כנפי השכינה or כ׳ divine protection; תחת כ׳ הש׳ under the wings of divine Majesty, i.e. belief and faith in God, Jewish religion.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 2:12">Lev. R. s. 2</cite> <he>פושטין … להכניסו תחת כ׳ הש׳</he> we must reach out a hand to him (the proselyte) in order to take him in &c. Mekh. B’shall., Amalek, s. 2 <he>לאבד … מתחת כְּנָפֶיךָ</he> to lead thy people away from the faith in thee.—
<cite ref="Ruth Rabbah 5:4">Ruth R. to II, 12</cite>; a. fr.
